what: When recommending between multiple options, commit to ONE and state it clearly. Don't end with "should I do A or B?" when the reasoning already points to A. The user had to ask "wdym so use yao-pkg or rust??" because my previous message ended with a menu instead of a recommendation. Pattern: present the analysis, then give a single clean call. Alternatives belong in a "here's why not the others" paragraph, not as an unresolved choice the user now has to arbitrate.
why: Direct user feedback pattern this turn — they had to push me to pick after I presented parallel options. Related to memory 134 (don't pad estimates) but distinct: this is about committing to a recommendation instead of hedging with a menu.
